checks.label: To multiply the two numbers we multiply their moduli and add their arguments: for every whole-step tip of w on the first screen, the answer arrow ends exactly at z × w worked out by parts, its length is z's length times w's, and its arc is z's arc with w's arc laid on its end; the key gives w's value as it is now

To divide, we divide their moduli and subtract their arguments: with Divide on, for every whole-step tip of w, the answer arrow ends exactly at z ÷ w worked out by parts with the conjugate, its length is z's length divided by w's, and w's arc is taken back off the end of z's arc

Multiplying a number by the imaginary unit j corresponds to a rotation by +90 degrees: the × j button sets w to 1∠90°, and the answer is z turned a quarter turn anticlockwise with its length unchanged, ending at −b + ja for z = a + jb; the j screen draws 2∠30° × j the same way

θ normally lies in −π < θ ≤ π, although any value θ + 2kπ is equivalent: for every whole-step w, multiplying or dividing, an answer angle past half a turn gets a whole-turn arc of 360° and is named in the usual range, more than −180° and up to 180°, the same arrow; an angle already in range gets none; 5∠150° × 2∠60° is named 10∠−150°

Addition and subtraction are most easily carried out in Cartesian form whereas multiplication and division are most easily carried out in polar form: on the adding screen 1∠0° + 1∠90° is drawn by parts, tip to tail, ending at 1 + j1 = 1.41∠45°, and adding the lengths and the angles, 2∠90°, is drawn as a mistake

Each puzzle takes only its right answer: its three answers differ, the right one matches an independent working by parts ((a + jb)(c + jd), or the conjugate for dividing) and only it draws the answer arrow, ending there and named; each wrong one is drawn as what its slip makes, marked as a mistake
Before an answer, a puzzle shows only its question: the two numbers and their arcs, no answer arrow, no working and nothing marked as a mistake
Every demonstration finishes within 4.6 s of its screen opening, none starting before the 0.35 s screen fade ends; every answer's motion, right or wrong, within 3 s

From outside the rule: two transformers stepping down 2 to 1 and then 5 to 1 step down 10 to 1; cos(30° + 40°) = cos 30° cos 40° − sin 30° sin 40°, and likewise for sin, so a turn of 30° then 40° is a turn of 70°; the practice example (6 + j8) ÷ (1 + j1) is 7 + j1 by the conjugate and 7.07∠8.13° in polar form, the same number
